concepts.title: Summary of the Story
concepts.definition: Twin Melodies follows two young string-instrument musicians - Shruti and Nabin - whose practice, rivalry and friendship build towards playing together; the story shows how two different temperaments can blend into one harmony, like a duet reaching its crescendo.
concepts.key_idea: Two players, two moods, one melody: harmony is earned through practice and patience.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe106.txt story sections (Shruti, Nabin, the music practice)

solution_steps.explain: Two young musicians with different styles share the stage of the story.
Differences in temperament test their partnership.
Understanding turns two melodies into one duet.

concepts.title: Language Study - Idioms and Figurative Phrases
concepts.definition: The chapter trains readers to separate literal from figurative language through phrases like bite the bullet, wearing a look of distress, lost in his thoughts and bring it up - idioms mean more than their words, and the musical glossary adds crescendo to the store.
concepts.key_idea: Idioms refuse the dictionary: bite the bullet is courage, not teeth.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe106.txt idiom practice and glossary (crescendo, bite the bullet)

solution_steps.explain: Check whether words mean exactly what they say.

concepts.title: Theme - Friendship, Practice and Harmony
concepts.definition: The story's theme is that music - like friendship - demands listening: ego must soften, practice must continue, and two distinct voices can create a richer music than either alone, the twin melodies of the title.
concepts.key_idea: Talent solo is good; talents in harmony are better - that is the story's music.
question_patterns: what is the theme of the story - explain

solution_steps.explain: Cooperation turns separate talents into harmony.
The duet finale embodies the lesson.
Teams, families and classrooms work the same way.
